headline: Funding flows. Launches resume. Hypersonics stall.
deck: This week sees a mix of funding successes and program delays, with some companies finally getting back to business.

stories.head: Blue Origin resumes New Glenn launches after investigation
stories.body: Blue Origin has completed its investigation into the New Glenn launch failure, allowing launches to resume. This comes after a significant delay, during which the company presumably avoided the phrase 'technical difficulties.' The New Glenn rocket is crucial for Blue Origin, which has invested over $2.5 billion in its development.
stories.soWhat: If Blue Origin can avoid future setbacks, they might just stay relevant in a market that’s increasingly unforgiving.

stories.head: Space Force awards $437M for satellite network
stories.body: The Space Force has awarded Viasat and SES a $437 million contract to build four small satellites aimed at enhancing military communications. This investment underscores the military's ongoing push for more robust satellite infrastructure, as the demand for secure communications continues to grow.
stories.soWhat: With military budgets expanding, companies that can deliver quickly on these contracts might find themselves in a very lucrative position.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense focus
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding is aimed at bolstering co-orbital security and space domain awareness, a hot topic given the geopolitical climate. The company is now well-positioned to capitalize on increasing defense spending.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash flow often trumps innovation, True Anomaly’s funding success might just set a precedent for others looking to ride the defense wave.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's Starship V3 performance review
watchlist.body: With SpaceX's first Starship V3 launch hitting most test objectives, expect scrutiny on its reliability as future missions loom.

watchlist.title: NASA’s reorganization impacts future projects
watchlist.body: NASA's recent reorganization could lead to shifts in project priorities, making it essential to watch how this affects ongoing missions.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic test delays continue
watchlist.body: With the third consecutive delay in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests, the focus may shift to more practical technologies in defense.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration
watchlist.body: The partnership between Anduril and L3Harris for a tactical SDA constellation could reshape the competitive landscape in military satellites.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.

tickers.note: Virgin Galactic remains under pressure as commercial spaceflight expectations continue to shift.
Lockheed Martin's stock is buoyed by defense contracts, with the Space Force's $437M award adding to its portfolio.
Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program highlights the stickiness of defense contracts in uncertain times.
Aerojet Rocketdyne's performance in upcoming contracts will be closely watched after recent funding rounds in the sector.
